subject.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session

question: Should persistent reply-session conflicts be allowed to abort competing work and retire the session runtime after transient backoff is exhausted, so the session can self-heal instead of remaining wedged?
rationale: Tests and live proof support the recovery, but choosing forced teardown over surfacing the exhausted conflict is an intentional session-state and delivery tradeoff that automation cannot authorize.

options.title: Accept bounded self-heal
options.body: Keep the one-time fenced teardown after retry exhaustion, accepting that an overlapping turn may be interrupted to restore the session.

options.title: Fail without teardown
options.body: Retain current main’s backoff-only behavior and surface the exhausted conflict, avoiding forced interruption but leaving persistent wedges unrecovered.

options.title: Require a narrower trigger
options.body: Pause the PR until recovery can distinguish a demonstrably wedged runtime from sustained legitimate session-store activity.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded self-heal
recommendation.body: Keep the one-time fenced teardown after retry exhaustion, accepting that an overlapping turn may be interrupted to restore the session.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent current-main conflict retry layer is the direct policy boundary this PR extends.
